name: guardian_skills_index
description: Registry of the skills the agent can load. It is rendered into the system prompt every turn, and each skill is opened with GuardianSkillRead.
data: [{"name":"xsoar_case_triage","displayName":"XSOAR case triage reference","category":"foundation","description":"Reference skill for triaging Cortex XSOAR incidents. Holds the lookup tables -- severity codes (1 Low · 2 Medium · 3 High · 4 Critical), status codes (0 Pending · 1 Active · 2 Closed · 3 Archived), and the common close reasons (Resolved / False Positive / Duplicate / Other) -- plus how to filter with `getIncidents`/`SearchIncidentsV2` effectively (open = active status), and the escalate-vs-close decision heuristics. Load this when you need the case codes or the triage decision rule without the full investigation lifecycle. Holds the per-severity COUNT recipe (read `total` per bucket, do not page-scan). This build runs natively inside XSOAR 6 (on-prem) only -- every command is a real command on this tenant, dispatched directly through GuardianToolBridge; there is no separate connector generation to detect. The skill body contains the mandatory investigation lifecycle: monitor (`getIncidents`/`SearchIncidentsV2`) -> fetch (the same commands filtered by id, + `getEntries`) -> research (your own knowledge, plus `GuardianKBSearch`/`GuardianDocsSearch` if present in your tool catalogue) -> enrich (the reputation commands `ip`/`url`/`domain`/`file` for verdicts, `findIndicators` for correlation) -> document (`GuardianCaseNote` for concise War Room notes) -> resolve (`setIncident` -- pass the incident version; `closeInvestigation` with reason + notes). Carries the status/severity code reference and the never-invent-IDs rule. **For a PURE READ-ONLY request -- list cases, show/summarize one case, count by severity, read the War Room, look up a value -- you do NOT need the full lifecycle: answer from the read commands (`getIncidents`/`SearchIncidentsV2`/`getEntries`/`findIndicators`), using `xsoar_platform_reference` for exact query syntax. Recording findings onto the incident (a War Room note, a verdict field) becomes mandatory the moment you enrich, decide a verdict, document onto the case, or mutate it.** This build runs natively inside XSOAR 6 (on-prem) only -- every command is a real command on this tenant, no separate connector generation to detect. Read-then-write -- read the case fully before mutating it. For an actual investigation, record findings as War Room notes throughout (`GuardianCaseNote`), and write the running verdict/confidence/blast-radius/ATT&CK assessment directly onto the incident's own custom fields (`guardianverdict`/`guardianconfidence`/`guardianblastradius`/`guardianattacktechniques`) via `setIncident` as your assessment evolves -- the incident IS the investigation record, there is no separate local store. Group related incidents via XSOAR's native linked-incidents mechanism. For a true positive, recommend containment (recommend-only, approval-gated) -- name the exact gated command, never auto-execute.
